claimNotes: TheSinging.Bible /facts (source 3) is still dated 'As of October 4, 2026'. It still lists 52,316 recordings (47,560 English plus 4,756 Spanish), 22 styles (20 English, 2 Spanish), 44 versions per chapter in male and female voices, the 'Singing Bible Edition' based on the BSB, 'AI-empowered technologies', free with no sign-up and no ads, and the launch, App Store, YouTube radio and Google Play dates (Aug 25, Sept 21, Oct 2 and Oct 4).

TheSinging.Bible /funfacts (source 7) still has 'Under 20 minutes of listening a day sings you through the entire Bible in one year' and 'Jonah is available as a sea shanty.' It says 'more styles are on the way', but no new count has been published.

The Music Bible homepage (source 6) counter still reads 38,556 Scripture Songs (data-to-value) and 14 Complete Bible Genres. Memorize, read-along lyrics and AI playlists are all still listed. The homepage now also shows a 'Listen on YouVersion' link and a countries-reached counter. We found no announcement of a formal YouVersion partnership, so nothing was added. The countries figure is geographic and must not be added.

The Music Bible /ai-transparency (source 2) still has, verbatim, the 'never use artificial intelligence to create songs that interpret, paraphrase, or extrapolate' pledge, 'occasionally, a word or phrase may be repeated', 'at least 100% accuracy', '750,000 words' and 'Suno and ChatGPT'.
Answered Faith (source 1): every quote used is still verbatim and there is no correction or editor's note.

Crosswalk (source 4): both Fiechter quotes and the 11 styles, 30,000+ songs, three Spanish genres and free on iOS and Android still match. The page shows only 'Updated Oct 08, 2026', with no correction.

Washington Examiner op-ed (source 5): the headline, author (Micah Fiechter) and Oct 11, 2026 date still match, with no correction. Minor metadata note: the source type is 'Official', where the run's fact-check suggested 'Opinion'. The outlet field already says 'op-ed by Micah Fiechter', so readers are not misled. Left unchanged.

Barna (source 8): 33% worship songs, 29% interpreting scripture, 64% small-group curriculum, n=442, online in December 2025, published Oct 6, 2026. There is no correction, and the page still does not mention sung Scripture.
Deseret News (source 10), ChurchLeaders (source 11) and Religion Unplugged/Baptist Press (source 12) all still support the issue's figures, dates and quotes, with no corrections.

Searches turned up no independent accuracy test or published error rate for either project, no reversal, and no new reporting since Oct 18. The issue's 'we found no published error rates' and 'no outside check' lines still hold.

Political/geography check: no place names or political framing in the body. 'NC Baptists' and 'Biola University' appear only as organization credits, and 'Spanish' refers to a language. 'Washington Examiner' appears only in the sources list, where outlet names are exempt. The ChurchLeaders event location and the Deseret note on majority-language dubbing are rightly left out. No removals needed.
